About & Guide — ClinVerify
Clinical Laboratory Verification Tool · HMR Medical Biochemistry
About ClinVerify

ClinVerify is an open-source, single-file clinical laboratory verification tool developed at Helse Møre og Romsdal HF (HMR), Department of Medical Biochemistry, Norway. It implements CLSI and EFLM protocols for method verification, precision assessment, bias evaluation, method comparison, and reference interval verification.

Developed for open-source publication on GitHub. Version 1.2.2.

Includes SheetJS Community Edition (xlsx.mini v0.18.5), Copyright © 2013–present SheetJS LLC, licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0). Bundled so that Excel import works without an internet connection.

Module Guide
Module Standard Purpose
M1 — Within-RunCLSI EP15-A3Within-run precision verification
M2 — Between-DayCLSI EP15-A3Between-day (within-laboratory) precision
Bias — IQCEP15-A3 §BiasBias estimation via internal QC
Bias — EQA/DKKEP15-A3 §BiasBias estimation via EQA/proficiency testing
EP09cCLSI EP09cMethod comparison: Passing-Bablok & Bland-Altman
Inter-InstrumentFraser 1999Inter-module/instrument comparison
LinearityCLSI EP06-Ed2 (2020)Linearity / analytical measuring interval verification (weighted least squares regression; deviation from linearity vs allowable deviation from linearity, with multiplicity-adjusted confidence intervals)
Mentor (Two-Point)Theodorsson 2012 · Kallner 2013Alternative comparison for analytes where classical method comparison is not feasible; more cost-effective and uses existing patient samples. Recalibration uncertainty is reported as expanded uncertainty (k=2, ≈95% CI); the original Kallner spreadsheet reports unexpanded uncertainty (k=1) in some cells — values differ by a factor of 2 but the underlying calculation is identical.
RI VerificationCLSI EP28-A3cReference interval verification
Built-in checks against the guidelines

The statistics below are computed from the published expressions rather than from tables copied into this program. Each check re-derives values the guideline itself prints, and runs every time this page is opened, so a discrepancy would be visible here rather than hidden in a result.

Entering Data

Every module accepts data by four routes. Nothing is uploaded to a server — files are read inside this browser.

  1. Type it in. Enter values directly in the module’s level / replicate grid.
  2. Paste from Excel (Ctrl+V). Copy the cells and paste them into the paste box of the module, in the layout you already hold them in — replicates across columns and levels down rows, or one measurement per row, depending on the module. No file needed.
  3. CSV file. Semicolon-separated, so that files exported by a spreadsheet set to a decimal comma (74,8) are read correctly without reformatting.
  4. Excel file (.xlsx). Parsed locally by a spreadsheet library bundled inside this page, so it works with no internet connection.
Templates. Each module offers a Simple template containing only the columns the analysis needs, and a Full template that also carries descriptive fields (sample number, date, analyte, unit, instrument, control material). On import only the value columns are required — every descriptive column is optional, and column headings are matched case-insensitively against a list of accepted alternatives, so an export from a laboratory information system rarely needs editing. Information already typed into the module header is not asked for again in the file.
Module Columns required on import Optional
M1 — Within-Run Value Level (omitted → all values treated as one level), sample no., date, analyte, unit, instrument, material
M2 — Between-Day Day, Value Level, Replicate, and the descriptive fields
EP09c X (Comparator), Y (Candidate) Sample no., analyte, unit, method names
Mentor (Two-Point) Method (Reference / Candidate), Level (Low / High), Value Sample no., analyte, unit, instrument names
Linearity (EP06) One line per level: X then the replicates, tab- or semicolon-separated —
RI Verification · Inter-Instrument A single column of values, pasted from Excel —
Custom TEa database Analyte, TEa_percent, Source —

Working across several analytes. Save / Restore stores the entered data, the selected criteria and the state of every module for all analytes in one portable file, so a verification study can be reopened and extended as further data arrive.

Demonstration dataset. The linearity module offers ⬇️ Demo dataset (CSV), which writes out the creatinine panel used by the built-in demo (six pools, duplicates, single run; synthetic data, not patient or quality-control results). The file is written in the layout this application imports, so it can be pasted or loaded straight back in and will reproduce the demonstration exactly — and the assigned concentration of each pool is stated in the file header for programs that ask for a nominal value rather than a mixing proportion. It is intended for checking that import works on your own machine, and for entering the identical panel into another program when results are to be compared.
Embedded Databases
  • EFLM_DB — Biological variation (CVI, CVG) with desirable imprecision and bias goals, 142 analytes
  • MANUFACTURER_DB — Manufacturer repeatability and within-laboratory imprecision claims taken from package inserts: Roche cobas c 303/503/703 and cobas e801, Sysmex XR-Series, InteRRliner, Tosoh G11, Siemens Atellica CH / NEPH, Siemens CS-5100
  • RI_DB — Reference intervals, 100 analyte / sample-type entries (NORIP, manufacturer)
  • TAE_DB — Total allowable error targets, 107 analytes across four selectable schemes: Nordic EQA (Labquality / NOKLUS / RfB / DEKS), CLIA 2024 (42 CFR 493), RCPAQAP 2022 and Rili-BAEK 2023. A laboratory-specific TEa table can also be imported from CSV.
Key References
  • CLSI EP15-A3. User Verification of Precision and Estimation of Bias, 3rd ed., 2014
  • CLSI EP09c. Measurement Procedure Comparison, 2018
  • CLSI EP28-A3c. Defining, Establishing, and Verifying Reference Intervals, 2010
  • CLSI EP06-Ed2. Evaluation of Linearity of Quantitative Measurement Procedures, 2nd ed., 2020 (replaces EP06-A, 2003)
  • Kallner A, Khorovskaya L, Pettersson T. A method to estimate the uncertainty of measurements in a conglomerate of instruments/laboratories. Scand J Clin Lab Invest 2005;65:551–558
  • Aarsand AK et al. The EFLM Biological Variation Database. biologicalvariation.eu [accessed 29.06.2026]
  • Fraser CG. Scand J Clin Lab Invest 1999;59:487–490
  • Theodorsson E. Validation and verification of measurement methods in clinical chemistry. Bioanalysis 2012;4(3):305–320
